text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Vietnam and Burma are determinied to strengthen their bilateral ties, Communist Party Secretary General said as he left Burma on Saturday.
-- President Le Duc Anh signed legislation on value added tax, corporate income tax, commercial law and amendments to the penal code.
-- The Vietnam Data Communication Company has opened a second gateway in Hanoi to access the ineternational Internet.
-- Ho Chi Minh City-based Viet Tien Garment Company has decided not to renew a $45,000 contract to use the trademark of the French fashion firm Pierre Cardin.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet concluded his visit to the Czech Republic and headed for Italy.
-- The government has decided to establish a strategy for the development of science and technology until the year 2020.
-- A South Korean plastic surgery delegation will carry out operations on 200-300 children with facial deformities in Hue from May 26 to June 5.
-- China beat Vietnam 3-1 in the World Cup Asian zone group eight qualifying match in Ho Chi Minh City on Sunday.

-- The Ministry of Trade invited Arthur Dunkel, former General Director of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) will act as a technical consultant to Vietnam during negotiations for joining the World Trade Organisation.

-- Joint-venture, 100-percent foreign-owned enterprises and foreign partners co-operating in doing business with Vietnam will be allowed to import cars and material for capital construction with tax exemption before July 1st, 1997.
